items.title: fix(fleet): quiet exit on broken pipe — SIGPIPE default + EPIPE-safe secrets output (#5569)
items.body: Fixes #5569 — `fleet secrets list | head` panicked with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe` when the downstream pipe closed early. ## What changed - **`crates/fleet/src/main.rs`** — restore the default SIGPIPE disposition at startup (`restore_default_sigpipe`, unix only). The Rust runtime ignores SIGPIPE, so a `println!` in *any* domain panics on EPIPE. With the default disposition the process dies quietly by SIGPIPE, like a well-behaved Unix filter, whichever verb is printing. This is the shared-path fix: the audit found no shared print helper — queue, search, and secrets each print independently — so the shared entry point is where the class is fixed. - **`crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs`** — `secrets list` and `secrets get` now write through a locked stdout with `writeln!`, classifying the outcome via `write_line`: BrokenPipe → quiet `EXIT_OK`; any other write error stays loud (`EXIT_UNRESOLVED` + stderr). Only EPIPE gets the quiet path — genuine write errors are not masked. - **`Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`** — `libc` as a unix-only direct dependency of the `fleet` bin (already in the lockfile as a transitive dep) for the disposition reset. ## Tests (oracle: writer outcomes + the binary's pipe behaviour) - New unit tests in `secrets.rs` with a failing-writer oracle: BrokenPipe maps to the quiet outcome, other errors (StorageFull) stay loud, and a successful write is byte-exact. `cargo test -p fleet --bin fleet`: **13 passed, 0 failed** (laptop). - Scripted repro on the built binary: `fleet --help | head -1` × 30 — **0 panics** (pre-fix this class panicked via `println!`; triage task 10082 reproduced the panic on `secrets list` itself, 1-in-10 racy). - `cargo fmt --check` clean. Local `cargo clippy` could not run to completion on the laptop due to a pre-existing stale-target toolchain skew (E0514 in untouched crates `fleet-config`/`fleet-proxy-proto`); CI's fresh clippy run is the check for that. ## Audit note (acceptance: other list-shaped verbs) Queue and search do **not** share the secrets print path (verified: independent `println!` sites in `fleet-queue`/`fleet-search`), so they did not share this exact defect path; the SIGPIPE disposition reset in `main()` covers their early-close behaviour when run through the `fleet` binary. Queue task 10517 (lane code-c), follow-up to triage task 10082. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.
